A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Discrete Guidance Matching work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–H support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original energy-guided simulations, sampling-time measurements, guided multimodal benchmark results and regularization ablations in Figures 2–3 and 5–12 and Tables 2, 3 and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation, multimodal evaluation and ablation results. Their retention from v1 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The posterior reweighting, Bregman loss, target-sample regularization and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. Section 3.4 now correctly describes the always-valid sampler already present in v1's Appendix A. Newly disclosed network architectures do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six synthetic 2-D distributions, source-to-target regularization example, GenEval generation task and SEED-based multimodal alignment. Evaluation coverage remains POPE, MME-P, MMB, GQA, MMMU and MM-Vet.

E2.justification: The simulations retain the Nisonoff et al. predictor-guidance comparator and the same rate-based and posterior-based variants. Comparator membership in Tables 2, 3 and 5 is unchanged. Newly cited related work is not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported simulation settings, initialization comparisons, guidance strengths, sampling steps, benchmark metrics and regularization sweeps are retained. The sample count, network specifications and schedule details added in Appendix H document existing experiments without revising previously stated settings.

E4.justification: The guidance-strength and initialization comparisons, 2-D regularization analysis, GenEval regularization ablation and qualitative multimodal examples are retained. v1's H.2–H.4 become v2's H.3–H.5; the inserted implementation subsection adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the original experiments. The point-estimate and graphical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All empirical entries in Tables 2, 3 and 5 and the plotted results are unchanged, including the proposed method's GenEval overall score of 0.78. The limited change concerns the computational comparison in Table 1 and Remark 1: v1 associates D+1 rate-based evaluations with masked initialization, whereas v2 associates this count with Algorithm 3 and assigns D(|S|−1)+1 to the cited Nisonoff implementation.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Theorems 1–2, Proposition 1 and their proof arguments are retained. Appendix E.1.2 makes an existing equal-kernel assumption and density-ratio substitution explicit without changing the derivation. The RLHF mathematics is relocated rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: exact general discrete guidance, one guidance-network forward pass per step, Bregman training with regularization, and effectiveness on energy-guided and multimodal tasks. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Table 1 and Remark 1 refine the efficiency explanation by tying the D+1 evaluation cost to the always-valid implementation rather than masked initialization. Interpretations of sampling accuracy, regularization benefits and applicability otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H substantially expands implementation documentation across both experiment families. New disclosures include three 256-unit SiLU hidden layers, 100,000 source samples and Adam with learning rate 1e-4; multimodal details specify six 768-dimensional LLaDA blocks, embedding sources, the L4 metric and the time schedule. v2 also states that implementation code accompanies the supplementary materials. These are disclosures, not established experimental changes.

R1.justification: Section 3.5 adds Rector-Brooks et al. (2025), on discrete denoising posterior prediction, when motivating preference alignment. The broader positioning remains unchanged. The additional Nie entry repeats an already cited work under different venue metadata, rather than introducing distinct research.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted prose and terminology edits, changes citations to author–year format, and moves the existing RLHF formulation from Section 4.2 into Section 3.5. It adds short acknowledgments, ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements while retaining the main narrative and most appendix organization.

P2.justification: The document-wide conversion to ICLR formatting changes typography, margins, headers and figure/table scale and placement. Table 1 moves into the introduction and gains a note; Table 5 is grouped with Figures 6–7, and Figures 10–12 now share one page. The underlying figure content and empirical table entries are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies previously missing architecture, training and probability-path details in H.1–H.2, improving reproducibility documentation. Its sampling-cost qualification and relocated RLHF formulation also improve clarity. The core theory and empirical evidence remain intact. Although the tighter layout makes some plots smaller, the documentation gains support a modest net improvement.
